projects.title: TARA — Identity Fraud Ring Detection Platform
projects.subtitle: TiT 6.0 Hackathon (Thrive-In-Tech), QoreID Track — full-stack build
projects.problem: Individual identity verification (QoreID) confirms a person is real, but passes coordinated fraud rings acting through multiple independently-verified identities — no single verification check catches a network of colluding accounts.
projects.process: Adapted an existing repo (VERA/GRACE, a financial transaction fraud detection backend) under explicit event permission, reusing the graph architecture but replacing the domain logic entirely — from transaction patterns to shared identity attributes (device, address, employer, signup timing).
execution: Built a 4-endpoint REST API (POST /identities/verify, GET /verdict/{id}, GET /graph, GET /health) with real QoreID integration — live BVN/NIN verification, token exchange with in-process caching (~55min TTL), and automatic graceful fallback to a deterministic stub on failure, transparently marked in every response so a demo never silently fakes a result.

Built three custom fraud-detection patterns: shared-attribute clustering (device/address/employer), identity fragmentation (fuzzy name-matching via RapidFuzz with a shared-context guard), and coordinated onboarding velocity (time-windowed device/referral clustering).

Built an explainable, additive trust-scoring engine — no black-box ML; every point on the score traces to a human-readable evidence string — hard-coded so the system can never auto-reject; max severity is "Review."

Built dual-layer persistence: an in-memory graph for detection-speed reads plus Postgres (SQLAlchemy, hosted on Aiven) for durable storage, with BVN-based idempotency to prevent duplicate identities on resubmission.
Wrote 10 automated tests covering every detection pattern and edge case — including a dedicated regression test asserting the system never hard-rejects.

Shipped a self-contained Docker image (supports local Postgres via docker-compose or a hosted Postgres target) deployed live on Render, with startup-time config self-healing (auto-corrects Postgres URL scheme mismatches and malformed QoreID base URLs instead of crash-looping).
results: 2nd Runner-Up overall, Winner — Digital Identity & Trust Track, TiT 6.0 Hackathon.
projects.reflection: Identity-fragmentation detection is O(n²) at current scale — fine for a pilot, with a specific fix path: attribute-bucketing to narrow comparison scope before applying fuzzy matching.

projects.title: Job Tracker — Microservices Application
projects.subtitle: Spring Boot microservices — User, Job, and Notification services
execution: Built a 3-service microservices architecture: User Service (registration, authentication, profile data), Job Service (job applications, interview scheduling, interviewer status updates), and Notification Service (Kafka event listener sending real-time notifications).
Implemented JWT authentication in the User Service, with tokens issued at login and validated across services via Feign.

Used Feign Clients for synchronous REST communication between Job Service and User Service, and Kafka for asynchronous, event-driven interviewer-status updates from Job Service to Notification Service.
Registered all services with Eureka Discovery Server and routed external requests through Spring Cloud Gateway.
